summary: Echelon Capital is evaluating Redwood primarily for cost-efficient production inference. They run a mix of low-latency chat (financial analyst assistant) and high-throughput batch embeddings. Key concerns: per-token unit cost, impact of batching and prefix/KV cache on effective unit economics, availability of dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, and enterprise security (KMS, VPC, SOC2). Redwood AE/SE covered hosted vs dedicated pricing buckets, caching and batching levers, and proposed a short benchmark pilot. Agreed next steps include pricing deck, security pack, and scheduling a benchmark with sample prompts.

Header: 2026-03-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Laura (Echelon Head DS), Ravi (VP Eng), Ben (Infra)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): Hey everyone, thanks for making time, appreciate it. Quick intro from our side, Maya is our solutions engineer, I'll handle pricing and next steps.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Laura): Hi all, Laura here. High level we're looking at inference for a trading assist product and batch embeddings for research. Main thing is cost, we have a pretty tight budget.
00:22 Speaker 1 (Samir): Totally. Could you run through volumes and latency SLOs? Even ballpark helps us model per-token costs.
00:33 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Sure — current prod mix is about 200k chat tokens/day, spikes to 1.2M during market open, and embeddings pipeline does roughly 20M embedding tokens/week. We're exploring 500M/month if feature goes prod. Latency target for chat is 200–400ms p95.
00:55 Speaker 2 (Maya): Good — so two distinct workloads: low-latency chat and high-throughput batch. They have different cost levers; batching helps embeddings a lot, caching/prefix reuse helps chat if prompts are templated.
01:10 Speaker 4 (Ben): Can you explain how caching affects costs? We heard about KV cache and prefix cache, but unclear how that reduces per-token.
01:20 Speaker 2 (Maya): Absolutely — quick high level: prefix caching stores the early layers/kvcache for repeated prompt prefixes so we don't recompute tokens on the left, so effective new tokens per request drop. With templated prompts we often see 30–60% token savings. KV cache (session cache) speeds up streaming and helps long-lived conversations by avoiding re-encoding. Batching groups independent requests into one kernel call which amortizes overhead; for embeddings batching can reduce per-embedding cost by 2-4x depending on GPU and model.
01:50 Speaker 3 (Ravi): So, pricing — what's hosted per-token and how does that compare to dedicated reserved pricing?
02:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): For hosted we have tiered per-token rates — for reference, small models and embeddings might be $0.0004 per 1k tokens at low tiers, larger gen models higher; but rather than raw numbers, important part is the effective per-token after batching and cache. Dedicated is structured as reserved capacity — monthly commit tied to GPU pool, which gives you predictable throughput and lower unit cost for sustained volume. We can put together a cost model with your volume numbers.
02:25 Speaker 4 (Ben): I guess the tricky bit is spikes — market open. How does dedicated handle bursts?
02:32 Speaker 2 (Maya): Dedicated has burst capacity options and autoscaling policies; you can reserve baseline throughput then allow for burst on demand — though bursts can be queued or routed to hosted fallback depending on policy. That has cost implications but maintains SLOs.
02:48 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Any hard numbers you can give now for 500M tokens/month? Even back-of-envelope.
02:55 Speaker 1 (Samir): Off the cuff — if your workload is embedding-heavy and benefits from batching, unit cost can be significantly lower on dedicated. For hosted, assuming moderate batching/cache, maybe $0.xx per 1k tokens — I don't want to quote wrong number without the model mix. We'll produce a spreadsheet with scenarios: different batching assumptions (no batching, moderate, aggressive) and caching savings.
03:20 Speaker 2 (Maya): Also quantization and model selection matters — using 8-bit quantized variants or open models gives you different kernel throughput and costs. We can recommend quantization profiles per workload.
03:32 Speaker 4 (Ben): On security — we need KMS integration, audit logs, and VPC peering. Are those available for hosted?
03:40 Speaker 2 (Maya): Hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS for encryption at rest and optional private network peering for Dedicated and Private options. Audit logs and RBAC are standard for enterprise tiers. For full on-prem or air-gapped, Redwood Private is the route.
03:54 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Would Private be necessary for PCI/regulatory? We're not PCI but we do have sensitive market data.
04:02 Speaker 2 (Maya): Likely Dedicated with VPC and customer KMS is enough; Private is for stricter requirements. We'll include a compliance mapping in the pack.
04:12 Speaker 5 (Laura): On the cost spreadsheet, can you model the effect of a 40% prefix cache saving on chat?
04:18 Speaker 1 (Samir): Yes, we'll show that — often chat sees big wins if prompts are templated. We'll show p95 latency impact too.
04:27 Speaker 5 (Laura): Also we run some LLM reranking for signals, small models but lots of calls. Those are latency sensitive.
04:35 Speaker 2 (Maya): Reranking usually benefits from small, quantized models on dedicated instances — very predictable latency. You can put rerank on a lower-cost pool.
04:45 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Benchmarks — we want a bench where you run our 50 canonical prompts at our target qps and measure p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens. Can you do that?
04:55 Speaker 1 (Samir): Yes — typical pilot: 2 weeks to set up, run with your prompts and show cost/latency with configuration variations (caching on/off, batch sizes). We'll need Ben's infra access for sample data transfer.
05:10 Speaker 4 (Ben): We'll provide a subset and a synthetic load generator. How intrusive is the benchmark? Do you need data in our VPC?
05:18 Speaker 2 (Maya): For hosted benchmark it's less intrusive; for Dedicated/Private we can run within VPC with customer-managed keys. We'll outline the tradeoffs.
05:28 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Onboard time for Dedicated — how long from commit to capacity?
05:32 Speaker 1 (Samir): Typical is 2–4 weeks depending on region and pool size; Private/on-prem is longer. We'll include timelines in the quote.
05:42 Speaker 5 (Laura): Any concerns about model drift / quality regression if you quantize?
05:49 Speaker 2 (Maya): We'll tie quality monitoring and evals to the rollout; Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles by workload and watches for regressions against your eval sets. We'll show sample eval results.
06:02 Speaker 4 (Ben): Do you provide per-route cost breakouts? We need to see per-feature economics.
06:07 Speaker 1 (Samir): Yes, Console gives token-level cost per route/model. That helps product decisions.
06:12 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Competitors — how is your price vs Anthropic / OpenAI for embeddings?
06:18 Speaker 1 (Samir): It depends on model selection. For embeddings OpenAI is a benchmark but once you factor batching and dedicated pools, our reserved pricing can be competitive. We'll include a competitor sheet but avoid publishing direct competitor pricing in the call.
06:30 Speaker 5 (Laura): Ok great. For next steps we'll need the pricing deck and a security pack, then schedule the benchmark. Who owns what?
06:38 Speaker 1 (Samir): Samir will send pricing + cost model; Maya will send security docs. Ben will send sample prompts and load profile. Laura will confirm pilot stakeholders and timeline.
06:48 Speaker 2 (Maya): Any other blockers?
06:50 Speaker 5 (Laura): No, just internal procurement timing. We might need a 30–60 day lead to lock a Dedicated commit.
06:58 Speaker 1 (Samir): Understood. We'll aim to support that. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by end of week with the materials and scheduling link.
07:08 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Thanks all.
07:12 [meeting end]
